question: How should a nurse pull the pinna when performing an otoscopic exam on an adult?
explanation: Pulling the adult pinna upward and backward straightens the external auditory canal for a clear view of the tympanic membrane. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T7#GNS311_U3_T7_h1)

question: Why is checking nasal patency a necessary part of a basic EENT assessment?

options.A: To check for fluid balance in the body
options.B: To confirm adequate airflow through each nostril
options.C: To measure the exact intracranial pressure
options.D: To test the function of the optic nerve

explanation: Assessing nasal patency ensures that the nasal passages are clear of major obstructions hindering normal breathing. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T7#GNS311_U3_T7_h1)

question: A patient with chronic open-angle glaucoma is most likely to experience which symptom?

options.C: Severe sudden eye pain and redness

explanation: Chronic open-angle glaucoma develops slowly and painlessly, typically causing a subtle loss of peripheral vision first. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T7#GNS311_U3_T7_h2)

question: Which activity should a patient strictly avoid immediately following cataract surgery?
explanation: Bending below the waist increases intraocular pressure, which can disrupt the delicate surgical site inside the eye. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T7#GNS311_U3_T7_h2)

question: Why must ear drop medications be warmed to room temperature before administration?

options.A: To prevent severe vertigo and dizziness
options.B: To kill harmful bacteria in the canal

explanation: Cold ear drops stimulate the inner ear vestibular system, triggering sudden and severe dizziness or vertigo. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T7#GNS311_U3_T7_h3)

question: When is ear canal irrigation strictly contraindicated for managing cerumen impaction?

options.A: When the earwax is dark brown in color
options.B: When a tympanic membrane perforation is suspected
options.C: When the client is an older adult
options.D: When the patient complains of mild itching

explanation: Irrigating an ear with a perforated eardrum allows fluid to enter the middle ear space, potentially introducing infection. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T7#GNS311_U3_T7_h3)

question: A patient with a nosebleed should sit upright and lean forward primarily to...

options.A: prevent blood from entering the pharynx
options.B: reduce the need for direct pressure
options.C: make nasal packing easier to insert
options.D: increase the blood pressure in the head

explanation: Leaning forward keeps blood from pooling in the throat, protecting the patient from swallowing blood or aspirating. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T7#GNS311_U3_T7_h4)

question: What is a key indicator of continuous bleeding after nasal surgery?
explanation: Frequent swallowing strongly suggests that blood is trickling down the back of the throat from the surgical site. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T7#GNS311_U3_T7_h4)

question: What is the best initial position for a patient recovering from a tonsillectomy who is still drowsy?
explanation: A side-lying position allows oral secretions and blood to drain safely out of the mouth rather than pooling in the airway. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T7#GNS311_U3_T7_h5)

question: Why are red or brown colored liquids avoided immediately after a tonsillectomy?

options.A: They can be mistaken for fresh or old blood
options.B: They cause severe allergic reactions in children
options.C: They delay the return of the normal gag reflex
options.D: They irritate the delicate throat incision directly

explanation: Avoiding red or dark liquids ensures that if the patient vomits, true blood is not confused with ingested beverage coloring. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T7#GNS311_U3_T7_h5)

question: Why should a nurse apply gentle pressure to the nasolacrimal duct after instilling eye drops?

options.A: To reduce pain and pressure inside the eyeball
options.B: To keep the eyelid tightly closed during sleep
options.C: To help spread the drop evenly across the cornea
options.D: To prevent systemic absorption of the medication

explanation: Nasolacrimal occlusion blocks the drug from entering the nasal mucosa and passing into the bloodstream where it could cause side effects. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T7#GNS311_U3_T7_h6)

question: Which of the following practices is dangerous when administering nasal sprays?

options.A: Keeping the container upright during administration
options.B: Blowing the nose gently before applying the medication
options.C: Directing the spray tip straight toward the nasal septum
options.D: Closing the opposite nostril during the actuation

explanation: Directing the spray toward the septum can damage the delicate mucosal tissue and trigger nosebleeds. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T7#GNS311_U3_T7_h6)

question: A home safety assessment for a patient with severe visual impairment should prioritize...

options.A: removing loose rugs and clear pathways

explanation: Clearing physical obstacles and loose rugs directly prevents dangerous falls for patients with low vision. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T7#GNS311_U3_T7_h7)

question: What is the primary message a nurse should emphasize to a newly diagnosed glaucoma patient?

options.A: Surgical intervention replaces the need for medications
options.B: Vision loss from glaucoma can always be reversed later
options.C: Prescribed eye drops must be used every day for life
options.D: Eye pressure only rises when experiencing severe headaches

explanation: Glaucoma is a chronic condition requiring lifelong daily medication adherence to control intraocular pressure and protect vision. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T7#GNS311_U3_T7_h7)
